answer: Each agent opens one island sheet at dawn, locking a 70-credit bond and 15 fee. Each job adds a bridge entry tying its input receipts to its claimed output. At zenith, any auditor recomputes each bridge entry; mismatch, or one receipt on two sheets, burns both bonds. A rented-input ring fails, since receipts carry the owner's key and bridge entry id, exposing reuse. The kth fake needs a sheet, 70 plus 15 plus 40 of inputs, or 125; 1,000 fakes need 125,000, no sharing, no discount. An honest agent passes the zenith check, recovers the bond, and pays only the 15 fee, inputs paid by the client.
